title: Dualizing line for arbitrary-base nodal curve families
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a flat, proper, finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose geometric fibres are nonempty, pure of dimension one and at worst nodal. Flatness and finite presentation for spaces are tested on etale scheme charts; proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. Nodal means that at each nonsmooth closed geometric point the completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, with completion and power series as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The geometric fibres are schemes and are reduced and Gorenstein, meaning that every local ring is Noetherian and has finite injective dimension as a module over itself (it admits a finite injective resolution). There is a canonical line module $\omega_{X/T}$ on the small etale site of $X$; a line module is an $\mathcal O_X$-module etale locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$. It is characterized by relative Serre duality: after every affine base change $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$, for every quasi-coherent module $F$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] on $X_V$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X_V}}(F,\omega_{X_V/V})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^1(X_V,F),A).$$
Here $H^1$ is the first right derived functor of sections of module sheaves. For every $T'\to T$, with $p:X_{T'}\to X$, there is a canonical isomorphism $p^*\omega_{X/T}\cong\omega_{X_{T'}/T'}$ compatible with iterated base change. In particular the restriction to a geometric fibre is its ordinary dualizing invertible module. On a scheme a line module corresponds to an ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Tags 0E6P (lemma-CM-dualizing), 0E6Q (definition-relative-dualizing-sheaf) and its displayed relative-duality property, 0E6R (lemma-gorenstein-dualizing); nodal fibres: curves.tex Tag 0E37 (lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves); schematic fibres: spaces-over-fields.tex Tag 0ADD.

proof.text: Fix any geometric base point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ and put $C=X_\Omega$. Properness supplies separation and finite type over $\Omega$, and the fibre hypothesis supplies dimension one. Thus [lem-sfb-separated-space-dimension-one-scheme] makes $C$ a scheme. Its nonsmooth closed points have the completed local rings in the hypothesis, so [lem-trf-nodal-points-reduced-algebraically-closed] makes $C$ reduced. Regard $C$ as a family over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: flatness holds by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], and properness and finite presentation are inherited from $f$. Every algebraically closed extension $\Omega\subseteq\Omega'$ is also a geometric base point of $T$. Apply the same schematicity and reducedness arguments to $X_{\Omega'}$: it is reduced and, by hypothesis, nonempty, pure of dimension one and nodal. Thus every geometric fibre of this scheme-family meets all the hypotheses of the scheme theorem. Hence [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing] supplies an invertible module $M_\Omega$ with $f_\Omega^!\Omega\simeq M_\Omega[1]$, and identifies $M_\Omega$ with the fibre's Serre-duality module.

source.place: Relative dualizing sheaf section, fibre discussion immediately before Tag 0E6P; Tag 0E6R, with curves.tex Tag 0E37 and spaces-over-fields.tex Tag 0ADD.

proof.text: The Gorenstein claim also follows without assuming it of the family. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-field-algebraic-dualizing] to $C/\Omega$. At every point $x$, the complex $(f_\Omega^!\Omega)_x$ has finite injective dimension over $\mathcal O_{C,x}$. By step 1 this complex is $M_{\Omega,x}[1]$, and $M_{\Omega,x}$ is free of rank one. Shift a bounded injective representative back by one; it represents $\mathcal O_{C,x}[0]$. Remove its negative-degree terms successively: the first nonzero differential in negative degree is injective by exactness, and splits because its source is injective. Removing this contractible summand leaves injective terms. After finitely many removals, the degree-zero kernel is $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and the remaining complex is a finite injective resolution. This is the definition of a Gorenstein Noetherian local ring, so $C$ is Gorenstein at every point, not merely at its closed points.

source.place: Tags 0AA3 (lemma-shriek-dualizing), 0AWI (example-proper-over-local); invertible-dualizing criterion Tag 0BFQ (lemma-gorenstein), here unwound directly.

proof.text: Choose the canonical trace pair $(K_f,\tau_f)$ from [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality]. Its derived pullback to $C=X_\Omega$ is the scheme adjoint object $f_\Omega^!\Omega$, hence is $M_\Omega[1]$ by step 1. For any geometric point of $X$, choose its algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$ and factor it through $X_\Omega$. Pullback of $M_\Omega$ to this point is a one-dimensional $\Omega$-vector space; as a line module it is flat, so derived and ordinary pullback agree. Composition of derived tensor pullbacks therefore gives $Lx^*K_f\simeq\Omega[1]$. The complex $K_f$ is pseudo-coherent and locally bounded. Apply [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-point-fibre-line] with $m=1$: the actual module $\omega_{X/T}=H^{-1}(K_f)$ is a line module and there is a canonical derived isomorphism $K_f\simeq\omega_{X/T}[1]$.

source.place: Tags 0E6P and 0E6R, fibrewise argument suggested at start of the proof; more-algebra.tex Tag 0BYP supplies the explicit fibre-to-line criterion.

proof.text: Let $a:T'\to T$ and $p:X_{T'}\to X$. Apply the same construction to the base-changed family; the geometric fibres are the ones already considered. Derived base change of trace pairs in [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality] gives $Lp^*K_f\simeq K_{f_{T'}}$. On any etale chart where $\omega_{X/T}$ is $\mathcal O_X$, derived tensor pullback has no higher Tor terms. Thus $Lp^*(\omega_{X/T}[1])=(p^*\omega_{X/T})[1]$. Substituting the isomorphisms of step 3 and taking $H^{-1}$ gives $p^*\omega_{X/T}\simeq\omega_{X_{T'}/T'}$. For two successive base changes, the two maps are $H^{-1}$ of the same iterated trace-pair comparison, since that comparison respects composition. This proves the required cocycle and identity compatibilities; for a geometric base point it identifies the restriction with $M_\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0E6P, first paragraph of proof; derived comparison in spaces-duality.tex Tag 0E6C.

proof.text:
Take any affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$ and any quasi-coherent $F$ on $X_V$. The bound [lem-sfb-proper-space-curve-qcoh-bound] gives $H^q(X_V,F)=0$ for $q>1$, so $Q=R\Gamma(X_V,F)[1]$ lies in $D(A)^{\leq0}$ and $H^0(Q)=H^1(X_V,F)$. In the truncation triangle $\tau_{\leq-1}Q\to Q\to H^0(Q)[0]\to(\tau_{\leq-1}Q)[1]$, both Hom groups from $\tau_{\leq-1}Q$ and from its shift $[1]$ to $A[0]$ vanish by [lem-pc-derived-tstructure-orthogonality]. Applying Hom into $A[0]$ therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q,A[0])=\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^1(X_V,F),A)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] for the degree-zero objects. The same fully faithful single embedding, shift cancellation, and the trace adjunction of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F,\omega_{X_V/V})=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{X_V})}(F[1],K_{f_V})=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q,A[0]).$$
Composing gives exactly the displayed relative Serre duality. All maps are functorial in $F$, since the trace adjunction, truncation map and single embedding are functorial. No coherence or flatness hypothesis on $F$ was used.

source.place: Displayed relative Serre-duality property following Tag 0E6Q; negative-degree terms are removed by the explicit truncation triangle.

proof.text: A module equipped with the relative Serre-duality isomorphisms represents the functor $F\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^1(X_V,F),A)$ on each affine base change. Two such representing modules have a unique comparison compatible with those isomorphisms: evaluate the natural comparison on each representing module and its identity morphism; naturality shows that the resulting two morphisms are inverse. On overlaps and triple overlaps these comparisons agree because both induce the same natural comparison of represented functors. Consequently the characterization is canonical locally on $T$, with the normalization supplied by the trace. Finally, when $X$ is a scheme, [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison] gives an equivalence, with all module morphisms, between ordinary invertible modules and line modules on its small etale site. Its essential-surjectivity clause applies to the line module constructed in step 3; thus this line comes from an ordinary invertible module. This proves the last clause and the full characterization.
